title: Fix duck timing for slow Piper TTS synthesis
description:
## Problem

On Raspberry Pi, Piper TTS synthesis takes 1-2 seconds. Current flow:

1. `speak()` called → `start_duck()` sets `duck_until = now + 1500ms`
2. Thread spawns → `tts.synthesize()` blocks for 1-2s
3. After synthesis → TTS audio plays

If synthesis takes 1500ms, the duck period expires BEFORE TTS audio starts.
Result: Channel announcements drowned out by stream.

## Solution

Move `start_duck()` call to AFTER `tts.synthesize()` completes, right before audio plays.

## Files to modify

- `src/audio.rs`: Pass `duck_until_ms` and `boot_time` to TTS thread, call `start_duck()` after synthesis

## Testing

Test on actual Pi hardware - verify TTS is audible over ducked stream.
close_reason: Refresh duck timer after Piper synthesis completes, before playing samples

title: Implement MultiStreamPlayer struct
description:
Create new MultiStreamPlayer struct to manage 4 simultaneous streams.

## Implementation

**File:** src/audio.rs

### New constant
```rust
const MUTED_VOLUME: f32 = 0.0;
```

### StreamHandle struct
```rust
struct StreamHandle {
    thread: JoinHandle<()>,
    stop_flag: Arc<AtomicBool>,
    sink: Arc<Mutex<Option<Sink>>>,  // For volume control from main thread
    status: Arc<AtomicU8>,           // 0=connecting, 1=playing, 2=error
}
```

### MultiStreamPlayer struct
```rust
pub struct MultiStreamPlayer {
    _stream: OutputStream,
    stream_handle: OutputStreamHandle,
    streams: [Option<StreamHandle>; 4],
    active_index: Option<usize>,      // None = all muted (Off state)
    duck_until_ms: Arc<AtomicU64>,
    boot_time: Instant,
}
```

### Methods to implement
- `new() -> Result<Self>`
- `select(&mut self, index: usize)` - switch active channel (volume-based)
- `start_duck(&self)` - duck all streams for TTS
- `speak(&mut self, text: &str, tts: &Arc<PiperTts>)` - fire-and-forget TTS, ducks all streams
- `speak_sync(&mut self, text: &str, tts: &PiperTts)` - blocking TTS

Keep existing Player struct for now, will migrate later.
